correctness.rationale: For any \(A,T>0\) and \(q_i\in(0,1)\) with \(e^{AT}Q>1\), \(1/S\) follows a positive affine period map of slope \(e^{-AT}/Q<1\). Pre-pulse heights lie in \((0,A)\) and are the between-pulse maxima. The exact cyclic flight identity gives \(\sum_i\log[(A-q_i s_i)/(A-s_i)]=AT+\log Q\); every summand is strictly increasing, forcing the unique lower peak \(M_*\) and equality at all \(s_i=M_*\). The uniquely recovered positive gap lengths sum exactly to \(T\). The strict commute inequality \(qF_t(s)<F_t(qs)\) bounds every return map by \(F_T(Qs)\), proving the sharp clustered supremum. Integrating \(\dot{\log S}=A-S\) plus pulse jumps yields the linear infection multiplier. The proof covers all finite pulse counts and positive gaps; 144 tests confirm sample cases but are not used for infinite scope.

value.rationale: For fixed prescribed vaccination coverage factors, identical Floquet growth rates conceal distinct susceptible peaks. This theorem completely solves the worst instantaneous vulnerability objective across all pulse placements: an explicit unique minimax (equal peaks), closed formula for optimal heterogeneous gaps, and sharp clustered opposite extreme. The gap objective is epidemiologically motivated independently of the known reproduction threshold. The result is not merely a re-expression of a one-pulse formula: the multi-pulse minimax and its extremal range require additional inequalities and generate nonuniform schedules for heterogeneous strengths.
